physical_scope: OS-managed keychain and configured access group
logical_contents: Passwords, OAuth tokens, refresh tokens, and credential material
retention_and_lifecycle: Retain while the account exists and delete explicitly with account removal
readers: Authentication services and authorized headless CLI or daemon
security_and_recovery_notes: Never copy secrets into Core Data, DuckDB, Parquet, logs, or exports; locked or unavailable access fails deterministically

physical_scope: One application-local persistent store with logical isolation by accountID
logical_contents: Account configuration, mailboxes, workflow plans/runs/tasks/attempts/dependencies, checkpoints, fetch operations, processing jobs/steps/results, leases, and DuckDB export checkpoints
retention_and_lifecycle: Retain active state and reusable results; prune only through explicit versioned retention policies and Core Data migrations
primary_input: User configuration and workflow subsystem state
writers: Core Data contexts owned by account workflow processing fetch and exporter services
readers: App CLI scheduler and diagnostic views
security_and_recovery_notes: Use one NSPersistentContainer with private-queue writer contexts indexed identities and an exclusive process writer lock; account rows are logically isolated and there is no direct SQLite access.

physical_scope: One DuckDB database beneath each account folder
logical_contents: Recent normalized email headers metadata and promoted analytical fields following email_metadata_parquet_columns.csv
retention_and_lifecycle: Keep open-period rows queryable until claimed for verified monthly archival
primary_output: Email metadata Parquet archive and analytical queries
readers: Library queries CLI exports and Parquet archiver
security_and_recovery_notes: Upsert by the durable mailbox message key using persisted globally allocated source revisions; Core Data and IMAP remain authoritative.

logical_contents: Stable terminal transformer results and typed analytical columns with transformer-specific JSON
retention_and_lifecycle: Keep recent rows until claimed for verified monthly archival
primary_output: Processing-result Parquet archive and analytical queries
readers: Library queries CLI exports and Parquet archiver
security_and_recovery_notes: Conflict key includes durable message identity, transformerName, and transformerVersion; replay after dual-store commit gaps is safe

logical_contents: Immutable email metadata and processing-result snapshots claimed for a specific archive batch
authority: Durable staging copy but not operational authority
retention_and_lifecycle: Retain through failures and restarts; delete only after verified Parquet publication and archive-manifest commit
readers: Parquet writer verifier diagnostics and logical analytical queries
security_and_recovery_notes: Archive batch IDs and source versions prevent live updates from mutating an in-flight snapshot

logical_contents: Dataset name archive batch state partition identity schema version expected batch count verified file row count Parquet path digest and commit timestamp
authority: Authoritative local record of downstream archive publication
retention_and_lifecycle: Retain committed manifests for audit and reconciliation
readers: Workflow coordinator diagnostics and repair tools
security_and_recovery_notes: Commit manifest and delete exporting rows in one DuckDB transaction

technology: DuckDB correction and tombstone table groups
logical_contents: Changes to metadata or processing results discovered after their monthly Parquet partition was sealed
retention_and_lifecycle: Retain until atomically compacted into the affected Parquet partition; preserve newer changes arriving during compaction
primary_input: Incremental sync reconciliation and processing-result corrections
primary_output: Queries merged with Parquet and later partition compaction
writers: DuckDBExporter sync reconciler and correction projector
security_and_recovery_notes: Use source versions and tombstones so stale archive data is never returned as current

physical_scope: One dataset partition per account mailbox and UTC calendar month
logical_contents: Normalized email headers metadata MIME structure provider fields and derived statistics
retention_and_lifecycle: Retain according to user archive policy; replace only through verified atomic publication or correction compaction
primary_output: Long-term queries CSV or JSON exports and backup
readers: DuckDB query layer CLI and external analytical tools
security_and_recovery_notes: Use schema_version, stable core columns, extensions MAP, verified row count, digest, and atomic rename

physical_scope: One processing-result dataset partition per account mailbox and UTC calendar month
logical_contents: Stable per-transformer processing results keyed separately from one-row-per-message metadata
retention_and_lifecycle: Retain with the corresponding email-metadata period; replace only through verified correction compaction
primary_output: Long-term transformer analytics joined to email metadata
readers: DuckDB query layer CLI and external analytical tools
security_and_recovery_notes: Preserve message join keys transformerName transformerVersion globally allocated sourceVersion and output schema version; use typed core columns and a Parquet MAP of canonical JSON extension values.

technology: Managed local files beneath each account folder
logical_contents: Normalized metadata-fetch results and large transformation outputs referenced by Core Data
retention_and_lifecycle: Retain while referenced by incomplete or reusable Core Data work; remove only after downstream acknowledgement and retention checks
writers: IMAP metadata fetcher and processing pipeline
security_and_recovery_notes: Store only relative locators and integrity fingerprints in Core Data; never place credentials here

technology: Managed local files beneath each account temporary-content folder
logical_contents: On-demand raw messages bodies MIME parts inline resources and attachments
retention_and_lifecycle: Delete on explicit release TTL expiry or active-fetch cancellation; while-in-use leases survive only their owning process session; clean up abandoned partial files after restart.
readers: Authorized caller during an active content lease
security_and_recovery_notes: Never treat as archive or processing source of truth; publish complete artifacts atomically and sanitize filenames
